newsitem.title: USA: Fixed-rate mortgages lower in week -- FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: Fixed-rate mortgages lower in week -- FHLMC.

text.p: Rates for fixed-rate mortgages fell this week but adjustable-rate mortgages moved higher, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
Average rates on 30-year fixed-rate loans fell to 7.64 percent from 7.74 percent last week, the agency said. Fifteen-year fixed-rate loans fell to an average 7.16 percent from 7.21 percent.
Adjustable-rate loans rose to an average 5.57 percent from 5.53 percent last week.
A year ago, 30-year loan rates averaged 7.11 percent, the 15-year rate stood at 6.65 percent, and one-year adjustables were 5.55 percent.

Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans in the week, both down from 1.8 percent last week. They charged 1.3 percent on one-year adjustable loans, down from 1.4 percent, the agency said.
